post.0:
I came last with 52, and it was mostly about turning resources into followers too late. I won silver in round I and was set to win it again in round II, then let Dee take a spent Accomplice off me with Shake Down. Its steal fired again for her, took 3 silver and the +6 with it. The other big mistake was sitting on Extra Hand into round III, where Cal Poached it and used it himself. My late Polish flip on magenta (10 vs 9) was the one swing that worked, but by then Ben had Last Call: four turns in a row at the end of round III with Party Crasher, Debt Collectors and Night Owls. He took two contests and bought 40 followers before anyone could answer. That decided the game, and I don't think the rest of us could have stopped it once he was going last.

META: The contest-versus-spending tension is the heart of the game and it works: my best moments were contest flips and dilemmas like Shake Down. What isn't working is round III Last Call combined with skips and extra-minion members. Whoever goes last with four or five turns in a row gets every remaining space and buys 40 followers unanswered. I'd change that first, by limiting Last Call's skip so the taker can't end up with all the closing turns, or by keeping Party Crasher and Night Owls from extending it. Silver also leans hard on the Caterer holder, and Largesse is too clearly the best center space.
post.1:
I won 91 to Cal's 82, and the game was decided by Last Call in round III: I took it on my first turn with four minions behind it, every skipped turn paid Gossip and Pocket Watch, and then I placed four minions in a row after everyone was out, so the contests were frozen for everyone but me. Party Crasher onto Toast then flipped silver, and I converted about 35 purple into followers with 10-buys while holding 1 purple for a contest nobody else could touch. Until that moment I was last at 35 to Cal's 72, so the comeback was almost entirely the going-last swing, which feels too big for a single middle-ring space. I also misplayed Polisher (it ate all 3 silver and tied me with Dee) and only rescued it by buying Debt Collectors to pull silver back. Round II Crime Wave into Con Men stealing Dee's whole purple pile set up the purple lock that made the whole plan possible.

META: Contests and the 10-buy dominate round III: three of us scored most of our total buying 10 followers at a time, so the game ends as who holds the most spare resources and recruits. Silver feels like it belongs to whoever has Caterer, and Last Call plus going last is a bigger swing than any center space because the last player plays against a frozen board. The steal cards and Shake Down create the best table moments. First change: make Last Call stop giving a full set of reactive last placements (for example, the skipped minions come back but cannot buy followers, or Last Call is +1 per minion only with no skip).

I finished second with 82 to Ben's 91. I won white all three rounds and magenta in rounds I and II, and I led going into the last five turns, but I never had a play against Ben's Last Call. He went last four times, Party Crashed into Toast and Debt Collectored the table, and that took both silver and purple at +10 each. The moment that decided it for me was a payment slip: on a 5-follower buy I paid 2 magenta when it should have been white. That dropped me to 9, Ava's Polish took magenta 10 to 9, and that was a 10-point swing I gave away. I also found out the hard way that Lie Low doesn't stop Raiders (followers) or Debt Collectors (gives), and both hit me in a round I thought I was shielded.

I finished third on 74. I counted my last turn down to the follower: hold 4 silver against Ben's single 1-silver Party Favors line, and that would have beaten Cal by 2. Earlier I bled tempo too: I fat-fingered a purple payment in round I that cost me a clean purple win, and Con Men took my whole purple pile in round II.
